content.user_title: Search bioRxiv Preprints by Topic or DOI
content.value_statement: Researchers need fast access to bioRxiv metadata without manual website searches. This skill searches the bioRxiv API and formats preprint metadata for review.
actual_capabilities: Searches bioRxiv preprints by keyword across title, abstract, or author fields.
Retrieves paper details by DOI from the bioRxiv details endpoint.
Filters date range searches by supported bioRxiv subject categories.
Downloads a selected preprint PDF to a user-provided path.
Saves structured results with DOI, title, authors, dates, category, abstract, and links.
limitations: Requires network access to api.biorxiv.org and www.biorxiv.org.
Keyword and author searches fetch date ranges first, so large ranges may be slow.
Uses simple substring matching and does not rank papers by relevance.
PDF download URLs assume version 1 and may fail for some records.

use_cases.title: Plan a literature review
use_cases.description: Find recent preprints in a defined topic, date range, and subject category before reading full papers.

use_cases.title: Track an author or lab
use_cases.description: Search recent bioRxiv records for a researcher name and review matching titles, dates, and DOIs.

use_cases.title: Build a preprint dataset
use_cases.description: Export bioRxiv metadata for trend analysis, citation preparation, or downstream data processing.

prompt_templates.title: Find Recent Papers
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the bioRxiv database skill to find preprints about CRISPR from the last 30 days. Include titles, authors, dates, DOIs, and links.

prompt_templates.title: Search by Author
prompt_templates.prompt: Search bioRxiv for papers by the author Smith from January 1, 2024 through December 31, 2024. Summarize matching papers with DOI links.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Category
prompt_templates.prompt: Find bioRxiv neuroscience preprints about neural organoids from 2024. Group the results by theme and flag papers with useful abstracts.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Research Dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Search bioRxiv for bioinformatics preprints about machine learning from 2020 through 2024. Save the metadata, limit results if needed, and summarize yearly trends.

output_examples.input: Find neuroscience preprints about neural organoids from 2024.
output: A concise result list with titles, authors, dates, categories, DOI links, and abstracts.
A short summary of recurring research themes across the returned papers.

output_examples.input: Track recent bioRxiv papers by a named researcher.
output: A filtered author match list with publication dates, DOI links, and paper titles.
A note when broad author names may match unrelated researchers.

output_examples.input: Download the PDF for a known bioRxiv DOI.
output_examples.output: A saved PDF file at the requested path and a status message indicating success or failure.

best_practices: Use narrow date ranges and category filters to reduce API calls and improve result quality.
Save results when repeating analysis so the same searches do not need to run again.
Review abstracts and links before citing because bioRxiv preprints can change or later publish elsewhere.
anti_patterns: Do not run broad multi-year keyword searches when smaller date windows would answer the question.
Do not treat preprints as peer-reviewed conclusions without checking publication status and evidence quality.
Do not download large PDF batches without additional delays and a clear research need.

faq.question: What sources does this skill search?
faq.answer: It searches bioRxiv through the public bioRxiv API and downloads PDFs from biorxiv.org when requested.

faq.question: Can it search by author name?
faq.answer: Yes. It fetches papers in a date range and filters records by case-insensitive author name matching.

faq.question: Can it filter by subject category?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports the bioRxiv categories listed in the skill documentation, including genomics and neuroscience.

faq.question: Does it include abstracts?
faq.answer: Yes. Formatted results include abstracts by default, along with DOI, title, authors, date, category, and links.

faq.question: Can it download full papers?
faq.answer: It can download a selected bioRxiv PDF when the prompt provides a DOI and output path.

faq.question: Does it work offline?
faq.answer: No. Searches and PDF downloads require network access to bioRxiv services.
